fluff.overview: The Hive-class drone fighters represent the Word of Blake's most ambitious unmanned aerospace program, drawing on Smart Robotic Control Systems technology retained by ComStar since the fall of the Star League. Designed as a coordinated suite of three complementary airframes, the Hive series was conceived to operate in self-supporting concert, with each design filling a distinct tactical role. Blakist engineers drew upon experience with ancient BlackWasp and VoidSeeker drones, as well as modern experimental Trident fighters, to create a new generation of unmanned combat aerospace vehicles optimized from inception for autonomous operation. Produced at Master's Wings Aerospace on Mars, the Hive fighters leveraged Terra's unmatched industrial base to incorporate technologies rarely seen on conventional manned fighters. The program produced three distinct designs: the light Tabanid interceptor, the medium Scarab fighter-bomber, and the heavy Aeshna strike fighter, each carrying specialized equipment that enhanced the effectiveness of the entire formation.
fluff.capabilities:
The Aeshna is the heaviest of the three Hive-class designs, carrying armor protection comparable to the most heavily plated fighters in production. Large variable-speed pulse lasers serve as primary weapons, their adjustable pulse rates providing consistent accuracy across all engagement ranges. A pair of ultra-class autocannons deliver devastating ballistic firepower, and a concentrated squadron of Aeshnas can tear through a DropShip's armor plating in just a few salvos. Dual extended-range lasers mounted in the nose round out an already formidable weapons suite, providing additional reach that complements the autocannons' raw destructive output.

Despite its heavy airframe, the Aeshna mounts a comparatively modest engine that limits its speed relative to the lighter Scarab. This trade-off prioritizes protection and firepower over maneuverability, a sensible approach for an unmanned platform where pilot survivability is not a design consideration. The fighter can carry a limited anti-ship missile loadout of two weapons, though its airframe could theoretically support a heavier bomb load. Heavy ferro-aluminum armor completes the design's emphasis on durability and sustained engagement, ensuring the Aeshna can absorb significant punishment while delivering its heavy ordnance on target.
fluff.deployment: The standard Aeshna represents the upgraded production model resulting from the early 3070s refit program. In addition to the heavy ferro-aluminum armor upgrade shared across all three Hive-class designs, the Aeshna received advanced variable-speed pulse lasers to replace its original laser systems. This exchange improved accuracy across varying engagement distances, complementing the heavy fighter's already formidable autocannon and missile armament. The refit gave the Aeshna a distinctly angular profile that has become the upgraded design's most recognizable visual feature.
fluff.history:
ComStar's centuries-long custodianship of Terran Hegemony technology ensured that Smart Robotic Systems, the sophisticated drone control architecture employed on Star League-era BlackWasp and VoidSeeker unmanned fighters, survived the Succession Wars intact. When the Word of Blake splintered from ComStar, it carried this institutional knowledge into its new order. Blakist aerospace engineers began preliminary design work on what would become the Hive-class drone fighters even before the Word had secured control of Terra, recognizing the potential for a new generation of unmanned combat vehicles built around an improved version of the original robotic control system.

Once the Word of Blake established its hold over Terra and gained access to the planet's vast manufacturing infrastructure, the program moved rapidly from concept to production. The facility on Mars received the contract to produce all three Hive-class designs, and the first operational units entered service in 3058. These original-production fighters were built along Star League-era design principles, employing conventional armor and weapons systems available at the time. The three designs proved the viability of coordinated drone fighter operations, with each airframe's specialized role complementing the others in ways that manned fighter wings struggled to replicate.

The Hive fighters saw their most significant evolution during a comprehensive refit program initiated in the early 3070s. All three designs received heavy ferro-aluminum armor, dramatically improving their survivability and giving them a more angular appearance that distinguished the upgraded airframes from their predecessors. The Scarab and Aeshna also exchanged their original laser systems for advanced variable-speed pulse lasers during this refit, significantly enhancing their combat effectiveness. These upgrades coincided with the Word of Blake's broader military buildup during the Jihad, as Blakist commanders sought every advantage their technological reserves could provide.

Following the fall of the Word of Blake at the conclusion of the Jihad, the Mars production facility passed into the hands of the Republic of the Sphere along with much of the former Blakist industrial base on Terra and its neighboring worlds. The facility's production status in the post-Jihad era remains uncertain, though the Republic inherited both the tooling and technical documentation for all three Hive-class designs.
